chapter: Alma Hightower and other women musicians
title: Lady Wilcar, outstanding pianist
summary: Collette and Howard praise Lady Wilcar, who played with Al Adams and George Brown's bands.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Own, you know, pleasure. Then,
later on, I know you remember this lady who was an excellent pianist who used to work with quite a few bands. Lady Wilcar(phonetic).
Oh, Lady Wilcar? Yeah.
Lady Wilcar used for us when we started playin' with you, with Al Adams and George Brown and--
Yep. Yep.
She was excellent.
She sure did.
Don't you remember?
Yeah.
What do you know about her?
What do I know about her (chuckle)? Lady Wilcar? She could play a piano, man.
Yeah (unintelligible)--excellent talent.
Excellent.

She could write, she had perfect pitch, you know--ears and everything, so that was when I remembered her as doing a lot'a work, lot'a recordings. And she could do it all as a pianist--classical, read, write--
Put it on that thing, there.
What's that?
Put it on that thing, there.
You know more about it than I do.

Well, that came later, so I was just wondering whether there were any others, you know, around that period when Alma was there that played--any other women that played instruments? That you could remember?
Well, Alma played with me for a long time, you know--
Uh-huh.
Different times, you know; you get out, you can play.
Sure.
I can't think of anybody else who played with us.
